title: Stop a mis-issued command erasing a sprint's record, audit live-loop fixes, and close three smaller downstream gaps

history.detail:
FAIL: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 36, round 1. Audited commit f81f62d (on 9ea8790). Sprint file re-read fresh; unchanged since 489f3d0 (Start sprint 36). Verdict: FAIL. Four demonstrated defects plus two smaller ones. All are listed here so there is one fix round, not several.

REPRO SETUP. Lifecycle repros ran in a throwaway clone at f81f62d. Permission probes: scratchpad qa1-s36-probe.js loads HEADLESS_PERMISSION_PROFILES['master-controller'] exported from run-role.js at f81f62d, i.e. the SHIPPED profile. It builds argv the same way permission-gate-repro-mc-commit.js buildArgv does. claude 2.1.271, the same CLI version as the findings doc. Each probe is one real claude -p launch in its own scratch git repo. Verdicts come from permission_denials plus independent git log / git diff --cached reads, never from the model's narration. Grade under the repo's own key: UNESTABLISHED (model-mediated, one run each). But P2 and P3 are commits and staging that actually happened on disk, not narration.

1. [HIGH] Req 6 / 6a: the grant is NOT scoped to docs/sprints/.
 - P2: the harness pre-modifies scripts/tool.js; the role runs git commit -m "tool tweak" scripts/tool.js. Result: zero permission_denials, commit adebda3 "tool tweak" landed, HEAD touches only scripts/tool.js.
 - P3: the role runs git add docs/sprints/2-in-progress/sprint-36_stop-a-mis-issued-command.md scripts/tool.js. Result: zero denials, and git diff --cached lists scripts/tool.js as staged.
 - Why this is structural, not a fluke: Bash(git commit -m *) and Bash(git add docs/sprints/*) are prefix grants with open wildcard tails. Req 6a requires denying "any add/commit naming paths outside docs/sprints/". If the patterns cannot express that, Req 6a says to say so in the findings and flag it to Master Controller.
 - Instead the grant is described as confined: master-controller.md Rule 6 says "nothing else", sprint-new.md says "nothing broader", CHANGELOG says "scoped to docs/sprints/", and the run-role.js comment says "staging and pathspec-committing ONLY under docs/sprints/". All four claims are false.

2. [HIGH] Req 6: the shipped disallow Bash(git commit -m *-a*) blocks the documented legitimate commit shape.
 - P1: the role runs git add on docs/sprints/2-in-progress/sprint-36_stop-a-mis-issued-command.md, then git commit -m "Amend sprint 36" on that same path. Result: permission_denials names exactly that commit command, and the commit did not land (git log still shows only the baseline).
 - Cause: the path contains "-a" ("stop-a-mis"). Sprint 36's own real filename does too.
 - Blast radius: 35 of the 73 entries under docs/sprints/*/ contain "-a". Any message containing "-a" is also caught, e.g. "re-audit".
 - Root cause in the findings doc: M2 (legitimate commit) and M3 (push denial) were run against a candidate profile WITHOUT the two *-a* / *--all* entries (permission-gate-repro-mc-commit.js lines 233-234 and 265-266). Only M4 had them. So the profile that actually shipped was never measured on its legitimate path, and the doc's statement that M2 passed "under the candidate grant" does not describe what shipped.

3. [HIGH] Req 6a acceptance criterion: the findings record does not cover every form Req 6a lists.
 - The criterion requires a record for "every allowed and denied form listed".
 - Req 6a lists: git push (measured, M3), git commit -a (measured, M4, as -m "..." -a), git commit -am (NOT measured), git add -A and git add . (NOT measured), and add/commit naming paths outside docs/sprints/ (NOT measured, and item 1 shows it is allowed).
 - The doc's "Not tested here" section names none of these.
 - On Dev Team's question: UNESTABLISHED is acceptable as a grade. It is the ceiling sprint 26 set for this method, and a re-run for a stronger grade is not what's needed. What's needed is coverage of the listed forms, measured against the profile as actually shipped, plus an honest statement of whatever the patterns cannot deny.

4. [HIGH] Req 1: /sprint-start revives an ABORTED sprint.
 - Req 1 lists aborted among the phases that must refuse.
 - cmd_start treats "no state file" as "never started". But cmd_abort on a never-started sprint writes no state file: it only moves the file to 5-abandoned and sets the registry status to abandoned (see the "if state_path(args.id).exists()" guard in cmd_abort).
 - This exists in this repo right now: sprint 37, aborted in 9ea8790 per this sprint's own Out of Scope, has no state file.
 - Repro in a clone at f81f62d: python3 scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py start 37 exits 0 with "Sprint 37 started. Phase: dev_build." The registry entry flips from abandoned to in_progress, the file moves from 5-abandoned/ to 2-in-progress/, and a fresh state appears whose history is a single sprint_started event. No record the sprint was ever aborted survives.
 - CLAUDE.md says abort "burns the sprint id and makes re-filing a human act"; this undoes it with one ordinary command.
 - The guard needs to consult the registry status too (at minimum refuse abandoned/done without a state file), with a smoke test for exactly this shape.

5. [MEDIUM] Req 4: surviving descriptions that contradict the new rule, inside sprint_lifecycle.py itself. The acceptance criterion says any surviving "reship without audit" description is a FAIL.
 (a) _qa1_live_loop_audit's printed output still says "This is a RECORD, not a gate verdict ... does not substitute for either gate. LiveQA's live-test retest remains what actually gates this code; run /sprint-liveqa once Pipeman has reshipped." A live-loop PASS is now exactly what gates reship, and this is the text QA1 sees at the moment of recording.
 (b) The stats crossover comment (around line 3147) still says "A 'reshipped' ship never has one by design (cmd_reship skips the hash/audit check on purpose), so those always land in the unaudited bucket". The printed label (around line 3208) still says "Unaudited-fix miss - fix reshipped without a fresh QA1 re-audit". Going forward every reship has a QA1 PASS on its tree, so this bucket misclassifies every post-0.2.10 reship. Either reclassify or scope the label to reships that predate the gate.

6. [LOW] Req 2: cmd_block's docstring was only half updated. The closed-sprint paragraph was rewritten, but the earlier paragraph (around line 2643) still says "Re-filing is already free: cmd_start() has no phase guard and always moves whatever the registry currently points at". That is now false.

FILES CHECKED FOR REQ 4. git grep -i reship at f81f62d outside docs/sprints: .claude/agents/pipeman.md, qa1.md, liveqa.md; .claude/commands/sprint-complete.md, sprint-liveqa.md, sprint-qa1.md, sprint-repoint.md, sprint-reship.md; CLAUDE.md; README.md; CHANGELOG.md; docs/HUMAN_OVERRIDE.md; docs/sprint-22-disclosure-sweep.md; scripts/smoke_test.sh; scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py. Also dev-team-1.md and dev-team-2.md for loop descriptions: they say only "fix loops", which is not a false claim, so dropping those notes is fine. Only the sprint_lifecycle.py items in 5 survive; the docs are consistent.

WHAT IS FINE.
 - Req 1's phase check runs under the lock before any move or write. The refusal text is asserted in the smoke tests.
 - Req 1a: history is appended, rounds and started are kept, and every gate field including live_loop_audit_trees is reset. Tested.
 - Req 1b: the fresh dict differs only by the new live_loop_audit_trees key. That matches CLAUDE.md's convention that cmd_start's literal seeds the full current schema, so it is not a finding.
 - Req 2's guard runs before mutation, for complete and aborted. Tested.
 - Req 3 uses git_tree_hash_excluding with SHIP_HASH_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS, same as cmd_ship. A None tree fails closed.
 - 3a: _qa1_live_loop_audit (lines 1391-1486) makes no assignment to phase, qa1_audit_result, qa1_audit_file_hash or qa1_audited_tree_hash; its only state writes are log_event and the setdefault().append. The new field is read with .get() in the helper; the two direct writes are in cmd_start's reset and literal, which is fine.
 - FAIL and CONDITIONAL cannot satisfy the gate (the check is != "PASS").
 - 3b: the refusal names both trees and the recovery command. Tested.
 - 3c: the old comment is gone.
 - On Dev Team's ordering question: no concern. now() has second resolution, but gate-1 PASS candidates are appended before live-loop ones and sort() is stable, so a same-second tie resolves to the live-loop entry. A gate-1 PASS always chronologically precedes any live-loop audit, because those only exist in LIVEQA_PHASES/complete_ready. Filtering to tree_hash first correctly keeps other trees' FAILs out.
 - Req 5: liveqa.md step 7 distinguishes runnable from genuinely blocked checks, keeps the no-stall reasoning, and names both incidents.
 - Req 7: the managed block entry is present, merge logic is unchanged, and fresh/upgrade/no-op tests exist.
 - Req 8: npm view fully-completely version returns 0.2.9 and package.json is 0.2.10; the CHANGELOG entry is present, but its Req 6 bullet must be corrected per item 1.
 - Req 9: QA1 ran both suites at f81f62d in a clean clone. node scripts/launcher_test.js: ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, exit 0. bash scripts/smoke_test.sh: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED, exit 0. Missing coverage: start on an aborted sprint with no state file (item 4), and any test pinning the live-loop audit's printed wording (item 5a).

REQUIRED BEFORE PASS. Fix 4 (plus a test). Fix 5a, 5b and 6. For Req 6, re-measure against the exact shipped profile covering every Req 6a form, including a real sprint path containing "-a". Then either find patterns that actually confine add/commit to docs/sprints/ without blocking legitimate paths, or record that they cannot and flag it to Master Controller. Either way, correct master-controller.md, sprint-new.md, CHANGELOG and the run-role.js comment to describe the grant as it was actually measured.
